passages.text: A wise son heeds his father’s discipline, but a mocker does not listen to rebuke.
passages.sermon: A wise son listens to his father’s discipline.\r\nA mocker does not listen to rebuke.
passages.original: בֵּ֣ן חָ֭כָם מ֣וּסַר אָ֑ב וְ֝לֵ֗ץ לֹא־ שָׁמַ֥ע גְּעָרָֽה׃

passages.text: From the fruit of his lips a man enjoys good things, but the desire of the faithless is violence.
passages.sermon:
A man speaks with his mouth.
His words can bring him good things.
A faithful man enjoys the results of his good words.
A faithless person desires violence.
The faithless do not seek good.
Their hearts long for harm.
passages.original: מִפְּרִ֣י פִי־ אִ֭ישׁ יֹ֣אכַל ט֑וֹב וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ בֹּגְדִ֣ים חָמָֽס׃

passages.text: He who guards his mouth protects his life, but the one who opens his lips invites his own ruin.
passages.sermon: A person who guards his mouth protects his life.\r\nA person who speaks carelessly brings ruin on himself.
passages.original: נֹצֵ֣ר פִּ֭יו שֹׁמֵ֣ר נַפְשׁ֑וֹ פֹּשֵׂ֥ק שְׂ֝פָתָ֗יו מְחִתָּה־ לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The slacker craves yet has nothing, but the soul of the diligent is fully satisfied.
passages.sermon:
A slacker is a lazy person.
A slacker wants things.
A slacker gets nothing.
A diligent person works hard.
A diligent person’s soul is fully satisfied.
passages.original: מִתְאַוָּ֣ה וָ֭אַיִן נַפְשׁ֣וֹ עָצֵ֑ל וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ חָרֻצִ֣ים תְּדֻשָּֽׁן׃

passages.text: The righteous hate falsehood, but the wicked bring shame and disgrace.
passages.sermon: A righteous person hates lies.\r\nA wicked person brings shame.\r\nA wicked person brings disgrace.
passages.original: דְּבַר־ שֶׁ֭קֶר יִשְׂנָ֣א צַדִּ֑יק וְ֝רָשָׁ֗ע יַבְאִ֥ישׁ וְיַחְפִּֽיר׃

passages.text: Righteousness guards the man of integrity, but wickedness undermines the sinner.
passages.sermon: Righteousness protects a person who lives with integrity.\r\nWickedness leads a sinner into trouble.
passages.original: צְ֭דָקָה תִּצֹּ֣ר תָּם־ דָּ֑רֶךְ וְ֝רִשְׁעָ֗ה תְּסַלֵּ֥ף חַטָּֽאת׃

passages.text: One pretends to be rich, but has nothing; another pretends to be poor, yet has great wealth.
passages.sermon:
Some people pretend to be rich.
They have nothing.
Other people pretend to be poor.
They have great wealth.
passages.original: יֵ֣שׁ מִ֭תְעַשֵּׁר וְאֵ֣ין כֹּ֑ל מִ֝תְרוֹשֵׁ֗שׁ וְה֣וֹן רָֽב׃

passages.text: Riches may ransom a man’s life, but a poor man hears no threat.
passages.sermon:
A rich man can use his wealth to save his life.
A poor man does not hear threats.
A poor man is not targeted for ransom.
Wealth can protect a person from danger.
Poverty can keep a person safe from certain dangers.
passages.original: כֹּ֣פֶר נֶֽפֶשׁ־ אִ֣ישׁ עָשְׁר֑וֹ וְ֝רָ֗שׁ לֹא־ שָׁמַ֥ע גְּעָרָֽה׃

passages.text: The light of the righteous shines brightly, but the lamp of the wicked is extinguished.
passages.sermon:
The righteous have light.
Their light shines brightly.
The wicked have a lamp.
Their lamp goes out.
passages.original: אוֹר־ צַדִּיקִ֥ים יִשְׂמָ֑ח וְנֵ֖ר רְשָׁעִ֣ים יִדְעָֽךְ׃

passages.text: Arrogance leads only to strife, but wisdom is with the well-advised.
passages.sermon:
Arrogance causes strife.
A proud person starts arguments.
Wise people listen to advice.
Those who seek counsel find wisdom.
passages.original: רַק־ בְּ֭זָדוֹן יִתֵּ֣ן מַצָּ֑ה וְאֶת־ נ֖וֹעָצִ֣ים חָכְמָֽה׃

passages.text: Dishonest wealth will dwindle, but what is earned through hard work will be multiplied.
passages.sermon: Dishonest wealth becomes less over time.\r\nHard work brings increase.\r\nWealth gained by honest effort grows.
passages.original: ה֭וֹן מֵהֶ֣בֶל יִמְעָ֑ט וְקֹבֵ֖ץ עַל־ יָ֣ד יַרְבֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but desire fulfilled is a tree of life.
passages.sermon: Hope that is delayed causes pain in the heart.\r\nA fulfilled desire brings life, like a tree full of fruit.
passages.original: תּוֹחֶ֣לֶת מְ֭מֻשָּׁכָה מַחֲלָה־ לֵ֑ב וְעֵ֥ץ חַ֝יִּ֗ים תַּאֲוָ֥ה בָאָֽה׃

passages.text: He who despises instruction will pay the penalty, but the one who respects a command will be rewarded.
passages.sermon: A person who despises instruction will suffer loss.\r\nA person who respects a command will receive a reward.
passages.original: בָּ֣ז לְ֭דָבָר יֵחָ֣בֶל ל֑וֹ וִירֵ֥א מִ֝צְוָ֗ה ה֣וּא יְשֻׁלָּֽם׃

passages.text: The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life, turning one from the snares of death.
passages.sermon:
A wise person teaches others.
This teaching gives life.
The teaching is like a fountain that gives water.
The teaching helps people avoid traps that lead to death.
passages.original: תּוֹרַ֣ת חָ֭כָם מְק֣וֹר חַיִּ֑ים לָ֝ס֗וּר מִמֹּ֥קְשֵׁי מָֽוֶת׃

passages.text: Good understanding wins favor, but the way of the faithless is difficult.
passages.sermon: A person with good understanding gains favor.\r\nA person who is faithless faces a hard path.
passages.original: שֵֽׂכֶל־ ט֭וֹב יִתֶּן־ חֵ֑ן וְדֶ֖רֶךְ בֹּגְדִ֣ים אֵיתָֽן׃

passages.text: Every prudent man acts with knowledge, but a fool displays his folly.
passages.sermon:
A prudent man uses knowledge.
A prudent man acts wisely.
A fool shows his foolishness.
A fool reveals his lack of sense.
passages.original: כָּל־ עָ֭רוּם יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה בְדָ֑עַת וּ֝כְסִ֗יל יִפְרֹ֥שׂ אִוֶּֽלֶת׃

passages.text: A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a faithful envoy brings healing.
passages.sermon: A wicked messenger brings trouble.\r\nA faithful envoy brings healing.
passages.original: מַלְאָ֣ךְ רָ֭שָׁע יִפֹּ֣ל בְּרָ֑ע וְצִ֖יר אֱמוּנִ֣ים מַרְפֵּֽא׃

passages.text: Poverty and shame come to him who ignores discipline, but whoever heeds correction is honored.
passages.sermon: A person who ignores discipline will become poor.\r\nHe will also experience shame.\r\nA person who listens to correction will receive honor.
passages.original: רֵ֣ישׁ וְ֭קָלוֹן פּוֹרֵ֣עַ מוּסָ֑ר וְשׁוֹמֵ֖ר תּוֹכַ֣חַת יְכֻבָּֽד׃

passages.text: Desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but turning from evil is detestable to fools.
passages.sermon: A fulfilled desire brings joy to the soul.\r\nFools hate to turn away from evil.\r\nTurning from evil disgusts fools.
passages.original: תַּאֲוָ֣ה נִ֭הְיָה תֶּעֱרַ֣ב לְנָ֑פֶשׁ וְתוֹעֲבַ֥ת כְּ֝סִילִ֗ים ס֣וּר מֵרָֽע׃

passages.text: He who walks with the wise will become wise, but the companion of fools will be destroyed.
passages.sermon:
A wise person has wisdom.
A fool lacks wisdom.
A person who spends time with wise people will become wise.
A person who spends time with fools will suffer harm.
passages.original: הָלוֹךְ אֶת־ חֲכָמִ֣ים וַחֲכָם וְרֹעֶ֖ה כְסִילִ֣ים יֵרֽוֹעַ׃

passages.text: Disaster pursues sinners, but prosperity is the reward of the righteous.
passages.sermon:
Sinners do evil things.
Disaster follows sinners.
Righteous people do what is right.
God gives good things to the righteous.
God rewards the righteous with prosperity.
passages.original: חַ֭טָּאִים תְּרַדֵּ֣ף רָעָ֑ה וְאֶת־ צַ֝דִּיקִ֗ים יְשַׁלֶּם־ טֽוֹב׃

passages.text: A good man leaves an inheritance to his children’s children, but the sinner’s wealth is passed to the righteous.
passages.sermon:
A good man gives an inheritance.
He gives it to his grandchildren.
A sinner gathers wealth.
The righteous receive the sinner’s wealth.
passages.original: ט֗וֹב יַנְחִ֥יל בְּנֵֽי־ בָנִ֑ים וְצָפ֥וּן לַ֝צַּדִּ֗יק חֵ֣יל חוֹטֵֽא׃

passages.text: Abundant food is in the fallow ground of the poor, but without justice it is swept away.
passages.sermon:
Poor people often have land that can produce much food.
This land is called fallow ground.
Fallow ground means the land is not being used.
There is much food in this unused land.
But sometimes, people lose this food.
They lose it when there is no justice.
Without justice, the food is taken away.
passages.original: רָב־ אֹ֭כֶל נִ֣יר רָאשִׁ֑ים וְיֵ֥שׁ נִ֝סְפֶּ֗ה בְּלֹ֣א מִשְׁפָּֽט׃

passages.text: He who spares the rod hates his son, but he who loves him disciplines him diligently.
passages.sermon: A father who refuses to discipline his son shows hatred toward his son.\r\nA father who loves his son disciplines his son with care and diligence.
passages.original: חוֹשֵׂ֣ךְ שִׁ֭בְטוֹ שׂוֹנֵ֣א בְנ֑וֹ וְ֝אֹהֲב֗וֹ שִֽׁחֲר֥וֹ מוּסָֽר׃

passages.text: A righteous man eats to his heart’s content, but the stomach of the wicked is empty.
passages.sermon:
A righteous man eats enough to satisfy himself.
A righteous man has what he needs.
The wicked have empty stomachs.
The wicked do not have enough food.
passages.original: צַדִּ֗יק אֹ֭כֵל לְשֹׂ֣בַע נַפְשׁ֑וֹ וּבֶ֖טֶן רְשָׁעִ֣ים תֶּחְסָֽר׃פ
